hook_text: The Moon does not really change shape. So why does it look like a banana one week and a ball the next?
clip_script: Durban. Night one: a thin silver crescent. Night seven: half a Moon. Night fifteen: a full Moon rising over the sea. Then it shrinks, night by night, until it is gone. Did the Moon change shape? No! It is always round. The Sun always lights half of it. As the Moon travels around the Earth, we see more or less of that lit half. New, crescent, quarter, gibbous, full. Every twenty-nine and a half days, it starts again.
visual_style: Whiteboard Moon diary with a row of circles shaded from dark, to a thin crescent, to half, to full and back again, then a lamp in the middle of a dark room with a learner turning a ball on a stick around her head.
mood: Patient and puzzle-solving, like cracking a secret code night by night.
pacing: First the Moon diary and the pattern, then the lamp and ball model that explains it, then the names of the phases and the 29 and a half day cycle.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and start your own Moon diary tonight.
